newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest bourse market cap to grow - bourse CEO.
newsitem.headline: Budapest bourse market cap to grow - bourse CEO.

text.p: The Budapest bourse, one of the world's best performers, says its equity market capitalisation as a percentage of gross domestic product (GDP) will grow substantially in the coming years.

Jozsef Rotyis, CEO of the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE), said on Wednesday he expected market capitalisation to rise to 20 percent in a few years from the current seven percent of GDP, catching up with the average ratio on emerging markets.
The BSE's market capitalisation was 733.08 billion forints at the end of October. Over the past year, the value of shares listed on the BSE grew by more than 100 percent in dollar terms.

Speaking at a two-day conference on Hungarian capital markets, Rotyis said he regarded the privatisation process, which is approaching its end, as a potential source of higher market capitalisation by helping new companies to go to the bourse.

Hungary's amended securities act, passed in November and becoming effective in January 1997, will also help ease the market's liquidity problems by obliging companies with a public offer of at least 200 million forints to seek flotation, he said.
